figures.finding: A feature must spend at least A$500,000 of qualifying Australian production expenditure to claim the Producer Offset, and above-the-line costs (development, the producers', director's, writers' and principal cast's pay) count only up to 20% of total film expenditure.
figures.applies: Australia, Producer Offset (ITAA 1997 Div 376), guidelines of July 2026 for projects starting principal photography on or after 1 July 2021; the 40%/30% rates are held in world.json and producer-calibration.

figures.finding: Screen Australia sets no percentage cap on producer fees in its Terms of Trade; the binding limit is the Producer Offset's 20% above-the-line cap, beyond which producer fees earn no offset. Its production funding over A$500,000 is a recoupable equity investment, the producer's Offset contribution must be at least 90% of the Offset's projected value for features, and once equity is repaid the producer takes 50% of profit.
figures.applies: Australia, Screen Australia Terms of Trade effective 4 December 2017 (current file, read 2026-11-01; the producer-calibration blocker found the older URL 404).

sources.said: Screen Australia production funding over $500,000 will be provided as a recoupable equity investment. … For Offset projects, that contribution will be at least 90% of the projected value of … Once all equity investment is repaid, the producer’s profit share will be 50%.

figures.finding: In 2024/25, 34 Australian theatrical features went into production for A$379 million (38 the year before); 14 of them cost A$1–5 million, eight A$5–10 million, five A$10–20 million and four over A$20 million; the Location Offset's rise to 30% from July 2023 drove a record A$1.0 billion from 20 international features.
figures.applies: Australia, Screen Australia Drama Report 2024/25 (published February 2026); features under A$1 million are captured retrospectively.

sources.said: A $379 million spend on 34 Australian theatrical features, up from $215 million on 38 titles in the prior year. … with the main concentration in the $1-5 million range — 14 of the 34 — two down on last year. … The number of features produced for over $20 million increased from one to four. Fewer titles were made in the $10-20 million range (five compared to last year’s eight) and the $5-10 million range increased from seven last year to eight in 2024/25. … driven primarily by the Location Offset increase to 30% from July 2023. … A record spend of $1.0 billion from 20 international shoot features.

figures.finding: Screen Producers Australia is the national body for independent screen producers; members pay a levy on each production, which counts as qualifying expenditure for the Producer Offset.

value.name: Screen Producers Australia
value.dues: levy per production (rate in SPA's levy statement, not read)

sources.said: As the national peak body for independent screen producers, SPA advocates for the issues that matter to the sector … SPA members contribute to the organisation’s advocacy and industry activities through a levy applied to each production, regardless of format or funding source. … The levy is included in the standard A–Z budget template and is recognised as Qualifying Australian Production Expenditure (QAPE) for the purposes of the Producer Offset.

figures.finding: Australia's Location Offset refunds 30% of a production's qualifying Australian spend for a feature, mini-series or TV drama series that spends at least A$20 million here (a series at least A$1.5 million an hour), and the PDV Offset refunds 30% of qualifying post, digital and visual effects spend of at least A$500,000.

value.excludes: documentaries (for features and mini-series), advertising, game and panel shows, public events, training films
value.law: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, Division 376, compilation in force 2026-10-01

figures.applies: Australia, any production company (Australian resident or with a permanent establishment and ABN) certified by the Arts Minister; the producer offset (Australian films) is held separately.
